_title: PDB + literature re-check of the blocked E3 recruiters, run to GRADE trigger TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE
_cost: $0 — CI fetch only, no GPU, no rental.
_why: The 2026-08-03 reopening scan surfaced two J Med Chem papers against TRG-E3-RECRUITER-STRUCTURE. That trigger's criterion is NOT 'a new ligand exists' — it is a deposited PARTNER-FREE LIGANDED structure for RNF114, DCAF16 or DCAF15, because the 2026-07-25 downselect found structural stageability, not ligand availability, to be what binds (e3-recruiter-downselect-2026-07-25.md section 5). The deciding fact is therefore a PDB census, not a paper, and it is free. This file is that census.

Both papers are PAYWALLED and only their ABSTRACTS were obtained; no claim here rests on unread full text.

dcaf16_cyanobenzothiazole.title: New Reversible Covalent Warheads: Cyanobenzothiazoles Recruiting DCAF16 for Targeted Protein Degradation.

preprint_search._reading: hitCount 1 = the journal record only; Europe PMC indexes preprints (source PPR) and returned none.

dcaf16_cyanobenzothiazole.abstract: Protein N-terminal cysteines (NCys) are valuable for selective modification and posttranslational regulation, but their proteome-wide landscape remains unexplored. We constructed a library of electrophilic probes, including cyanobenzothiazole (CBT), to systematically map ligandable native NCys residues. Modifiable NCys sites were identified in proteins such as GFPT1 and CSTB, revealing accessible NCys in the human proteome. Integrating CBT into a BRD4-targeting ligand generated a reversible covalent degrader (DC 50 = 16.7 nM, D max = 98%). Mechanistic studies showed that CBT modifies DCAF16 at Cys58, promoting ternary complex formation and enabling efficient ubiquitination and degradation. The platform achieved potent and selective degradation of challenging targets like EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S and HER2 without hook effects, outperforming clinical inhibitors. This work provides the first proteome-wide map of ligandable NCys residues and establishes CBT as a versatile platform for covalent targeted protein degradation (TPD), opening new avenues for precision therapeutics.

fem1b_dual_site.title: Structure-Guided Discovery of Novel Dual-Site FEM1B Ligands and Assessment of Their Use in Targeted Protein Degradation.

preprint_search._reading: hitCount 1 = the journal record only; Europe PMC indexes preprints (source PPR) and returned none.

fem1b_dual_site.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) represents a promising approach for eliminating disease-causing proteins beyond traditional inhibition. However, the reliance on a limited number of E3 ligases remains a major bottleneck. FEM1B, an E3 ligase substrate receptor with multiple substrate-recognition modes, represents an attractive but underexplored TPD platform. In this study, through a structure-guided approach exploiting the spatial proximity between a druggable C-degron-binding pocket and a second binding site containing a reactive cysteine, we developed FL47 , a dual-site ligand that combines extensive noncovalent interactions with targeted covalent engagement. FL47 exhibits submicromolar affinity, robust cellular target engagement, and markedly reduced cytotoxicity relative to previously reported covalent recruiters. We further applied FL47 in the development of FEM1B-based PROTACs and incorporated a chemical endocytic prodrug strategy that markedly enhanced degradation activity. This work introduces a novel dual-site binding strategy for E3 ligase ligand discovery and broadens the potential toolbox for TPD applications.

grade.roadmap_row: nr4a3-program-map.md section 6b — 'E3 recruiter breadth beyond CRBN + VHL' (R9, R12)
grade.why: The row's criterion is a deposited partner-free liganded structure for RNF114, DCAF16 or DCAF15. Measured today: RNF114 0 entries (HTTP 204), DCAF16 3 entries all ternary (n_clean_binary_entries = 0), DCAF15 9 entries unchanged. The DCAF16 paper is by its own abstract a template-assisted covalent GLUE mechanism — the cyanobenzothiazole sits on the BRD4-targeting ligand and 'modifies DCAF16 at Cys58, promoting ternary complex formation' — which is the SAME architecture the 0.3442 buried fraction described, not a refutation of it. More DCAF16 binders was never the blocker.
grade.evidence_level: PROVISIONAL on the paper text (abstracts only); DEFINITIVE on the PDB census.

fem1b_finding._correction: FEM1B IS one of the 10 recruiters the parked row assessed — it is not a new candidate. It PASSED all three gates (G1 on 9PW8 @ 2.8 A with ligand A1CLY; G2 buried fraction 0.8694; G3 clearance 25.0 A, 30-degree cone openness 0.5429) and was dropped on the PARETO front, at linker_analogue_tier 1 and open_solid_angle_fraction_15A 0.0449 — the tightest exit in the panel. Its drop reason was never structural stageability, so the trigger's criterion does not apply to it at all.
fem1b_finding.what_the_paper_would_bear_on: linker_analogue_tier only. Tier 1 means 'no SOLVED linker-bearing structure', and e3-recruiter-downselect-2026-07-25.md section 8 states that limit explicitly: 'A tier-1 recruiter is "no solved linker-bearing structure", not "no linker chemistry exists".' The paper reports FEM1B-based PROTACs built on a dual-site ligand FL47, i.e. exactly the linker chemistry that limit anticipated — but it deposited nothing, so the structurally-defined tier cannot move.
fem1b_finding.what_would_actually_move_it: A deposited FEM1B entry carrying a >=500 Da linker-bearing ligand. That is a DIFFERENT criterion from this trigger's, so it is given its own trigger rather than folded in: TRG-FEM1B-LINKER-BEARING-STRUCTURE.
fem1b_finding.what_it_does_NOT_touch: open_solid_angle_fraction_15A = 0.0449, the axis FEM1B actually lost on. Nothing in an abstract can change a measured solid angle, and a new conformer would have to be re-measured.

consequence_honestly_stated: Even a full REOPEN would hand a new recruiter to R9 and R12, both of which are 'future — NOT STARTED' and sit downstream of failures that are architectural rather than about recruiter choice. emc-post-degrader-options.md section 0 splits the programme into an ASSET (the ligandable cryptic NR4A3 pocket) and a LIABILITY ('the degradation geometry — ternary, E3, exit vector, ubiquitin transfer, and a ~1 kcal/mol paralogue margin'). The E3 recruiter is on the LIABILITY side. So this trigger, as worded, reopens a parked row inside a programme parked for unrelated reasons. It is kept because a partner-free DCAF16 or RNF114 structure would still be a real field advance worth recording — but a hit on it does not by itself restart any work, and the trigger now says so in its own metadata rather than leaving a reader to infer it.
